transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Claire (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Priya (Aurelius Procurement), Ethan (Aurelius Legal), Janelle (CTO), Samir (Security)

Summary: quick preflight for procurement and security acceptance. Focus: SSO/SAML flow, KMS integration (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), DPA/MSA redlines, SLA tiers for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing buckets and cost guardrails for pilot.

[00:00] Claire (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, we'll keep it tight. quick intros?
[00:12] Priya (Aurelius): hi Priya, head of procurement, I'll be owning commercial intake, thanks.
[00:18] Ethan (Aurelius Legal): Ethan here, legal counsel, focused on DPA and MSA redlines.
[00:22] Janelle (CTO): Janelle, CTO, I'll be scoped on private deployment and perf.
[00:28] Samir (Sec): Samir, security architect, will validate KMS/SSO/VPC requirements.
[00:33] Miguel (Redwood SE): miguel here, I'll cover technical acceptance and the micro-benchmarks. some network things up front?
[00:38] Claire: cool, agenda is SSO/KMS preflight, DPA/MSA Qs from legal, pricing buckets for pilot, then next steps.

[03:05] Priya: procurement wants a clear acceptance checklist: what documentation do we need to close the pilot? specifically encryption, data residency and egress fees.
[03:22] Claire: high level: SOC2 + ISO docs, KMS integration patterns (BYOK via customer KMS, or Redwood-managed with HSM), details on data retention and deletion, and SLA matrix. we'll send a one-pager.

[05:10] Ethan: on the DPA, two items: 1) audit rights timing, 2) subprocessor list and notification cadence. also want to see encryption at rest details. sometimes the transcribed names in the portal are off, so please send source artifacts.
[05:35] Miguel: noted. on encryption: for Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and we also have a Redwood-managed option for hosted. there are differences: BYOK keeps keys in your account and we never see raw key material. that addresses some of the audit concerns.

[07:40] Janelle: for our use case we need the KV cache persisted for active sessions but we can't have the keys leave our control. BYOK seems necessary. do you support HSM-backed keys?
[07:55] Miguel: yes, we support HSM-backed keys through KMS providers. small caveat: cross-region key usage can add latency, we'll note recommended region co-location.

[09:30] Samir: network: we need to understand what egress IP ranges to allow, is there a static set for Dedicated vs Private?
[09:42] Claire: Dedicated gives predictable egress ranges; Private (VPC) sits in your peered VPC so egress is within your network. we'll provide the CIDR / IP ranges and peering guidance.

[11:01] Ethan: SLA: what's the difference between your hosted API SLA and the Dedicated reserved capacity SLA? we need commitment for p50/p95 latencies for inference and separate SLO for throughput.
[11:20] Miguel: more or less: hosted has best-effort with commercial credits for downtime; Dedicated has a contractual uptime SLA (we publish latency SLOs for model classes, e.g., transformer-7b family p95 < 400ms for typical 256 token requests). these are model and config dependent. we can provide a performance profile for the exact model you want in the pilot.

[13:05] Priya: on pricing — we need a pilot figure: committed vs on-demand. procurement prefers a small reserved pool to get stable pricing with a defined ramp. is there an option for a month-to-month reserved pilot?
[13:22] Claire: yes, we offer short reserved pilots (1–3 months) for Dedicated with prorated terms. pricing tiers: reserved baseline, overage per token, and optional burst credits. we'll share a spreadsheet with examples for your workload distribution.

[15:00] Janelle: Miguel, we'd like to run a 48-hour micro-benchmark using a 512-token median prompt mix and our embedding workload, to validate latency and token cost. what data do you need?
[15:12] Miguel: ideally a sampled prompt set and expected concurrency. for private testing we can run against a masked dataset, or you can host a subset in a staging bucket and we'll point the runner. I can spin up a dedicated pool with the model and config used in production.

[17:30] Ethan: DPA questions: retention windows, deletion process, and legal hold. we may request a clause around flowdown obligations to subprocessors. also need to see a list of subprocessors and subcontracts.
[17:50] Claire: we'll include the current subprocessor list. note subprocessors change quarterly; we publish notices. for legal hold we have deletion APIs and retention policies that can be set per-tenant.

[20:05] Samir: curious about logs and audit: can you provide immutable audit logs for key management events and token-level usage with user IDs? that's important for compliance.
[20:22] Miguel: yes, the Console provides per-token breakdown and trace hooks. for Private we can ship logs to your SIEM via forwarders or S3 buckets, and key events are recorded and can be exported. small caveat: very verbose token-level exports can be large; we'll propose retention/aggregation that meets compliance without huge storage costs.

[22:40] Priya: are there any standard redlines Redwood refuses for MSA or DPA? procurement needs to know redline friction.
[22:55] Claire: typical: we accept most DPA redlines but have firm positions on indemnity carve-outs and export control. for MSA we avoid long open-ended liability; we can escalate any specific ask to legal—we'll be transparent.

[25:10] Miguel: technical note: for cost controls we recommend prefix caching and request-level quotas; that reduces token usage on repeated prompts. Also quantization profile can reduce GPU time cost by ~20–30% for certain models.
[25:38] Janelle: are quantized models functionally equivalent? we need quality gating.
[25:45] Miguel: there is a small delta; Redwood Optimize can run evals on your prompts and give quality vs cost tradeoff. we'll include an eval result example.

[28:03] Ethan: one procedural question: do you require e-signature for DPA or is email acknowledgement sufficient for pilot?
[28:12] Claire: for pilots we often do email acceptance; for production we require signed DPA/MSA. legal can accept an interim addendum if needed.

[30:00] Priya: procurement checklist request: provide a 1-pager with acceptance criteria for pilot (latency, availability, log exports), a sample pricing sheet, and contact points for escalation.
[30:15] Claire: yes we'll assemble that.

[32:20] Samir: technical preflight — we want a runbook for onboarding including SSO SAML metadata exchange, KMS key grant steps, network peering steps, and a rollback plan. can Redwood supply a templated runbook?
[32:36] Miguel: we have a runbook template; we'll tailor it and include exact API calls for key rotation and deletion. note: rotating customer keys requires re-encrypting caches, we document a safe sequence.

[35:11] Janelle: on data residency: our cardholder processing must remain in eu-west-1. can Dedicated be pinned to a region?
[35:22] Miguel: Dedicated capacity can be regionally pinned and we can restrict fallbacks. for Hosted we route by policy but you can request region pinning in the enterprise plan. we'll note data residency options in the one-pager.

[37:05] Ethan: on subprocessors — if Redwood uses a GPU infra partner, will that partner sign flowdown agreements?
[37:18] Claire: yes, for enterprise we require flowdown and can reference the latest subcontractor agreements. we'll provide redacted examples.

[39:30] Priya: timeline — procurement wants pilot start by Aug 2. realistic?
[39:40] Claire: yes if we get DPA + basic commercial terms signed by July 26 we can start onboarding first week of Aug. Miguel: from a technical side 7–10 business days to provision and run the micro-bench if we get creds and sample data quickly.

[42:02] Miguel: quick recap on benchmarks: I'll run a 48-hr job, produce p50/p95 latencies, token cost estimate and memory footprint. will share a CSV and spreadsheet.
[42:15] Priya: for pricing please highlight reserved vs on-demand delta and an example of a small reserved pilot.

[44:20] Claire: next steps recap: we'll share SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS integration note, the runbook template, pricing spreadsheet, and Redwood's subprocessor list. customer to send DPA questions by 7/20 and Samir to send network egress ranges.
[45:05] Ethan: quick clarification — can we get a contact in Redwood legal for redline discussion?
[45:12] Claire: yes I'll include Lydia Park (Redwood Legal) in the DPA email thread.

[46:00] Priya: thank you, that's helpful.
[46:05] Janelle: thanks, we'll review and aim to reply with DPA points this week.
[46:12] Claire: great we'll get material out today. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts mentioned: Redwood SOC2 summary (link: /redwood/soc2-summary.pdf), Redwood KMS integration note (link: /redwood/kms-integration.md), pricing spreadsheet (link: /redwood/pricing/aurelius-pilot.xlsx)
